grades.quote: The medium-priority thread is blocking the low-priority thread by virtue of their relative priorities. The low-priority thread is blocking the high-priority thread by holding the mutex.
grades.reason: Directly explains how a low-priority thread holding a mutex forces a high-priority thread to wait, and how medium-priority threads extend that delay (priority inversion).

grades.quote: it guarantees that a high-priority thread will only have to loan its priority to at most one lower-priority thread to free up a needed mutex.
grades.reason: Only auxiliary notes on solutions to priority inversion (priority inheritance, priority ceiling). It does not explain why a low-priority thread delays a high-priority thread through a lock.

grades.quote: Two forms of interaction, known as priority inversion and the convoy phenomenon, are particularly interesting.
grades.reason: Section introduction that names priority inversion as a synchronization–scheduling interaction. It gives no mechanism involving a lock.
